    “A greatsword forged in the likeness of the moon-eating serpent. Drained of all colour, it keeps the light it swallowed, and gives it back as a crescent.”

    The Eclipse-Bringer Greatsword is a Somber-upgraded Greatsword in Elden Ring. It deals split damage, part physical and part Magic, and it carries Frostbite buildup on every hit. Its unique skill, Moon-Devouring Tide, coats the blade in eclipsed moonlight and turns fully charged heavy attacks into straight-line Magic crescent waves.

    This guide goes over everything you need to know about the weapon: how to get it, what it does, its strengths and weaknesses, and what it takes to upgrade. By the end you will be carrying a greatsword forged in the likeness of a moon-devouring serpent, and a hard-hitting weapon that works both up close and at range.

    Why use the Eclipse-Bringer Greatsword?

    It is a good weapon when you want to deal real damage both up close and from a distance. Raise your Strength and Intelligence, and use talismans such as Godfrey’s Icon (raises charged spells and skills by 15 percent), Shard of Alexander (raises skill damage by 15 percent), and the Magic Scorpion Charm (raises magic attack by 12 percent but makes you take 10 percent more physical damage) to push your damage as high as it goes.

    Its special ability, Moon-Devouring Tide, costs 34 FP and gives +55 magic attack power for 45 seconds. It also turns a fully charged heavy attack into a ranged wave that applies 83 Frostbite buildup from up to 18 metres away. You do still need to respect its limits: the 1.8 second cast, the slow heavy attack, the 12.0 weight, and the 34 FP cost. With good positioning and the right talismans, you can stagger enemies, set Frostbite, and win fights on your own terms.

    The short reason Most Intelligence greatswords put most of their damage into Magic. This one keeps 54.6 percent of its 436 attack power in physical damage, and still fires Magic waves from range. Several late bosses block 40 to 80 percent of Magic damage. A magic-heavy greatsword loses that damage outright. This one does not.
    What you are giving up It is heavy at 12.0, the cast takes 1.8 seconds with no hyper armour, and you must raise both Strength and Intelligence. It rewards a player who plans the fight before it starts, not one who wants a light and fast weapon.

    Quick requirements

    What you needValueWhy it matters
    Starting classPrisoner or Astrologer Both start with high Intelligence, the stat the weapon scales with best.
    Rune Level to startAbout 105 two-handed, 111 one-handed The level where the requirements and a safe Vigor pool both fit.
    Strength18, or 12 if you two-hand it Two-handing counts Strength at 1.5 times its value, so 12 becomes 18.
    Dexterity12A hard requirement. Cannot be skipped.
    Intelligence30 The main damage stat. It scales at grade B at +10.
    Vigor40 or moreYou will be hit during the 1.8 second cast.
    Mind17 or moreEnough FP for the 34 FP cast plus flasks.
    Endurance22 or moreCarries the 12.0 weight and keeps the roll fast.
    Equipment loadUnder 70 percent Over 70 percent you fat roll. Over 100 percent you cannot roll at all.
    FP for one cast34Only the activation costs FP. Waves cost stamina.
    Buff length45 secondsCast again every 45 seconds.
    Passive effectFrostbite buildup 38 Does not rise with upgrades. Only the skill raises it.
    Upgrade pathSomber Smithing Stones, +0 to +10 One stone per level. An Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone for +10.
    Best fighting range8 to 18 metres Closer than 8 and the charge will not finish. Past 18 and waves fall short.
    Before the questDo not enter the Altus Plateau yet Touching it starts the Radahn Festival early and Ranni leaves her tower.

    Why these guide sections were chosen

    This page covers two things and leaves the rest to the full wiki entry.

    1. How to get the weapon. It sits at the end of one of the longest quests in the game, and one wrong step in the middle ends it for good. Nothing about the weapon is useful until it is in your hands, so this comes first.
    2. How to use the weapon. The skill is a timed buff, and the waves only come from a fully charged heavy attack. Most new players cast the buff, walk into a crowd, and never fire a single wave.

    Upgrading is folded into the second section rather than standing on its own. It only matters here through the damage of the waves, so a separate level-up page would just repeat the Somber stone list that any Elden Ring page already gives.

    Boss move lists and player-versus-player counters were left out. Those are already covered by the Elden Ring Wiki, and they make a beginner page longer without making it more useful.

    Before you begin

    The weapon comes from the Moon-Eater’s Hollow quest in Liurnia of the Lakes. It runs next to Ranni the Witch’s own quest and uses the same route.

    Where to startDetails
    RegionLiurnia of the Lakes, the north-west corner, at the Three Sisters
    LandmarkRanni’s Rise, the tallest of the three towers
    Site of GraceRanni’s Rise, once you reach the top
    TimeAbout three to five hours for a new player

    What you need before step 1

    • Reached Liurnia of the Lakes, which means Stormveil Castle is behind you.
    • Beaten Royal Knight Loretta at Caria Manor. This opens the road to the Three Sisters.
    • Not yet set foot on the Altus Plateau. If you do, the Radahn Festival starts early and Ranni will not be in her tower.
    • Rune Level 70 or higher, with your main weapon at +6 or better.
    • A few blue flask charges. The fights on this route are long.
    • Preserving Boluses or the Flame, Cleanse Me incantation. You will cross the Lake of Rot.
    • The Magic Scorpion Charm from Seluvis, if you plan to use it. Handing in the three Tide-Worn Scales ends his quest for good.

    How to obtain the Eclipse-Bringer Greatsword

    There are 13 steps. Follow them in order. The two marked with a warning are the ones that end the quest if you get them wrong. The full page, with troubleshooting, is at Moon-Eater’s Hollow.

    1. Go to Ranni’s Rise and agree to serve Ranni the Witch. Three Sisters, north-west Liurnia. Climb to the top and say yes. Result: Ranni takes you into her service.
    2. Talk to all three of her servants before you leave. Iji, Blaidd, and Seluvis are downstairs. Talk until their words repeat. Result: the barrier comes down and fast travel works again.
    3. Defeat Starscourge Radahn in Caelid. Redmane Castle, the Radahn Festival. Result: the stars move again and one falls into Limgrave.
    4. Climb down into Nokron, Eternal City. Crash site south of Mistwood. Result: you arrive in Nokron.
    5. Find the three Tide-Worn Scales in the Night’s Sacred Ground. Under the huge skeleton statue. Result: you hold three Tide-Worn Scales.
    6. Hand the three Scales to Ranni. Result: she gives you the Carian Inverted Statue and leaves.
    7. Open the moon-phase seal and enter Renna’s Rise. Jump the rooftops and rocks to the next tower, then take the waygate at the top. Result: you arrive at the Ainsel River Main.
    8. Wake the doll. Pick up Miniature Ranni in the water, rest, and choose “Talk to miniature Ranni” three times. Result: she sends you after the shadow.
    9. Defeat the Bakunawa Shade. On to the Nokstella Waterfall Basin, where the Moon-Eater’s Hollow opens off the river. Result: Miniature Ranni hands you the Discarded Palace Key.
    10. Open the chest in the Raya Lucaria Grand Library with the Discarded Palace Key. The chest is next to Rennala. Result: you get the Bakunawa Fang.
    11. Cross the Lake of Rot. On to the Grand Cloister and ride the stone coffin. Result: you reach Astel.
    12. Beat Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, then pass the seal. The Bakunawa Fang opens the sealed exit behind him. Result: you come out on the Moonlight Altar.
    13. Give the Fang to Ranni at the Cathedral of Manus Celes. Drop down the hole near the Site of Grace and follow the tunnel. Result: the Eclipse-Bringer Greatsword is yours at +0.

    How to equip and upgrade the weapon

    Meet the requirements

    The weapon asks for Strength 18, Dexterity 12, and Intelligence 30. If any is too low, the numbers show in red, swings come out weak, and the skill will not fire.

    Shortcut Hold the weapon in both hands. The game then counts your Strength at 1.5 times its value, so Strength 12 is enough. On a controller, hold triangle or Y and press the right bumper. On a keyboard, hold the left mouse button and press E.

    Watch your weight

    The weapon weighs 12.0. Keep your total load under 70 percent.

    Load readingWhat happensWhat to do
    Light, under 30 percentFastest roll, longest distance Good, but needs very light armour.
    Medium, under 70 percentNormal rollThis is what you want.
    Heavy, over 70 percentSlow fat roll Raise Endurance, or wear lighter armour.
    Overloaded, over 100 percentCannot roll or run Take something off at once.

    Upgrade it to +10

    The weapon uses Somber Smithing Stones and stops at +10. One stone per level, which is much cheaper than normal weapons.

    StepStone you needWhat you get
    +1 to +9Somber Smithing Stone 1, then 2, and so on to 9 Physical rises from 98 to 213, magic from 78 to 178.
    +10Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone Physical 238 and magic 198, for 436 total attack power.

    Travel to the Roundtable Hold, speak to Smithing Master Hewg, and choose Reinforce Armament. Repeat until the weapon reads +10.

    Warning Do not spend normal Smithing Stones on this weapon. They will not work. It only takes Somber stones.

    What the weapon will not do

    • It cannot take an Ash of War. Its affinity is fixed.
    • It cannot be buffed by sorceries, incantations, or greases. Its own skill is the only buff it takes.
    • Its Frostbite buildup stays at 38 at every upgrade level. Only the skill raises it.

    How to use Moon-Devouring Tide

    Full skill page: Moon-Devouring Tide.

    1. Cast before the fight starts. L2 or LT on a controller, right mouse button on a keyboard. Cost 34 FP.
    2. Wait out the 1.8 seconds. You cannot act during it.
    3. Check the blade. The groove must be glowing cold white. No glow means the buff is not on.
    4. Move to 8 to 18 metres. The band where a full charge finishes before the enemy reaches you.
    5. Hold the heavy attack button all the way. Do not let go early.
    6. Release at full charge. One wave flies straight ahead. 24 stance damage, 83 Frostbite buildup, stamina only.
    7. Watch the glow. When it pulses you have about five seconds. Make space and cast again.
    Warning Never cast while something is swinging at you. The 1.8 second activation has no hyper armour. Do not stow or swap the weapon while the buff is on. Both end it at once.

    Troubleshooting

    Getting the weapon

    ProblemLikely causeWhat to do
    Ranni is not at Ranni’s Rise The Radahn Festival has already started. It starts as soon as you touch the Altus Plateau or use the Grand Lift of Dectus. Check Redmane Castle. If the festival is running, beat Radahn first and come back. Ranni returns after he falls.
    You cannot reach the Three SistersCaria Manor is still sealed. Beat Royal Knight Loretta at the end of Caria Manor.
    The chest in Nokron will not open You have not agreed to serve Ranni yet. Go to Ranni’s Rise, enter her service, and come back.
    The seal on Renna’s Rise is still up The three Tide-Worn Scales have not been handed in. Take the Scales to Ranni first. The seal clears only after she has them.
    You cannot find the way into Renna’s Rise It is not entered from the ground. Leave Ranni’s Rise and jump across the rooftops and rocks.
    Miniature Ranni says nothing useful You have not spoken to her three times. Rest at the Ainsel River Main Site of Grace and pick “Talk to miniature Ranni” three times.
    The chest next to Rennala is locked Rennala is not beaten yet, or the key is missing. Beat Rennala at the Grand Library, then open it with the Discarded Palace Key.
    The exit behind Astel is sealedYou do not have the Bakunawa Fang. The Fang opens that seal. Do not go past Astel without it.
    Seluvis is suddenly a puppet Handing in the Tide-Worn Scales ends his quest. Get the Magic Scorpion Charm from him before you hand them in.

    Using the weapon

    ProblemLikely causeWhat to do
    The skill will not fireUnder 34 FP, or a requirement is not met. Drink the blue flask and check Strength, Dexterity, and Intelligence.
    Swings are weak and drain stamina A requirement is short, so the game applies a penalty. Two-hand the weapon, or raise the stat that is short.
    No wave comes outThe charge was not full. Hold the heavy attack button longer.
    The wave missesThe target moved, or the ground is sloped. The wave does not track and does not aim up or down. Lead the target.
    The buff ended earlyYou stowed the weapon or swapped. Keep it in hand.
    Frostbite never triggers The frost window is still open, or fire cleansed it. Wait out the 30 seconds, and keep fire away from the target.
    You are rolling slowlyCarrying too much. Raise Endurance, or use Great Jar Arsenal or Erdtree’s Favor.
    You keep dying during the castYou cast while the enemy was attacking. Cast before the fight or during a long recovery.
    The weapon takes no Ash of WarIts affinity is fixed. Nothing is wrong. Somber legendary weapons work this way.

    Notes and trivia

    • The weapon is drained of all colour, which is taken from the Eclipse Shotel’s own line about “an eclipsed sun drained of color.”
    • The guard and the split pommel are both built as an open serpent jaw, so the weapon shows the same shape at both ends.
    • The dark groove down the blade, called a fuller, is the only part that lights up while the skill is on. At five seconds left it pulses.
    • The cast sound carries a swell of distant drumming. That comes from the recorded practice of making noise during an eclipse.
    • The seven moons were cut down to the seventh moon alone, the one that got away.
    • Frostbite stands in for the earthquakes, rain, and wind of the popular retellings, because frost is already the game’s cold status effect.
